title: Nuclear power for Australia
log: 2026-11-02T06:24:51Z review: rejected, to be written again

rejected.title: Nuclear power for Australia
card: Nuclear power stations use fission to heat water into steam, which turns turbines. Running one produces very little carbon dioxide, and it can supply steady power day and night.
Nuclear plants are expensive and take many years to build. Australia has no nuclear power stations, so it would also need new laws, skills and regulators.
Used fuel stays dangerously radioactive for a very long time and needs safe long-term storage. Rare accidents can release radioactive material and harm people and the environment.
Physics can give facts about costs, risks and benefits. Deciding whether Australia should build nuclear power also involves values, such as how much risk people accept.
rejected.remember: Nuclear power gives steady, low-carbon electricity, but it has high costs and waste and safety risks to weigh.

a.q: Which is a benefit of nuclear power compared with a coal power station?
opts: It produces very little carbon dioxide while running
It is cheap and quick to build in a new country
It produces no radioactive waste at all
It cannot be affected by any accident
a.why: Fission heats water without burning fuel, so running the plant gives off very little carbon dioxide. The other options are wrong because nuclear plants are costly and slow to build, and they make used fuel that stays radioactive.
a.clue: Think about what is burnt in a coal station and what is not burnt here.

b.q: A Victorian council argues that Australia should build a nuclear plant because it is the right thing to do. Which part of this argument rests on a value judgement rather than physics?
opts: That building it is the right thing to do
That fission releases energy to heat water
That used fuel stays radioactive for a long time
That a plant can supply steady power day and night
b.why: Whether something is the right thing to do depends on what people value, such as how much risk they accept. The other three are facts about how nuclear plants work, and they can be tested with evidence.
b.clue: Which statement could not be settled by measurement alone?
